M.Cr.C.(A) No. 878 of 2023
  Ramesh Kumar Jangid S/o Shri R.S. Jangid, aged about 41 years, R/o
 H.No. 300/1/13, Balco Nagar, District Korba (C.G.)

---- Applicant
 Versus
  State of Chhattisgarh, Through : Station House Officer, Police Station Balco,
 District - Korba (C.G.)
 ---- Respondent/Non-Applicant
For Applicant : Mr. Abhishek Singh, Advocate
For Respondent/Non-Applicant : Mr. Vimlesh Bajpai, Govt. Advocate

For Objector : Mr. Sourabh Dangi, Advocate
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey
 Order on Board
18.08.2023
1.

The applicant has preferred this first bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. as he
apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No. 298/2023 registered at Police Station - Balco
Korba, District Korba (C.G.) for an offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of
Ipc.
2.

Prosecution case is that the complainant Narendra Tiwari lodged a report with the concerned Police Station alleging that he was an employee of the Balco and till January 2023, he was also an office bearer of the Trade Union, Balco.
Members of the said union and others had contributed in the account of the said trade union.

Accused G. Sanjeeva Reddy, Chairman of the Management Committee; Sanjay Singh, Executive President; Jai Prakash Yadav, General Secretary and Ramesh Jangid (present applicant herein), treasurer in a fraudulent manner have withdrawn the amount from the funds of said union and caused loss to the said organization.

It has been further alleged that as per the by-laws of the trade union, 3 persons namely, Jai Prakash Yadav, the present applicant and the complainant were authorized to withdraw the amount from the account, which was being maintained at Chhattisgarh Rajya Gramin Bank.
In pursuance of the direction of the Chairman and the Executive President, any of the two persons could withdraw the amount.

Jai Prakash and the present applicant, without the knowledge of the complainant, withdrew certain amount from the account and they did not furnish details of the expenditure, though the Ramesh Kumar Jangid vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131028426/
1 complainant was one of the signatories for withdrawal of the amount.

sentences.text: On query, Jai Prakash and the present applicant gave vague reply that they had withdrawn the amount as per the direction of co-accused Sanjay Singh.

On coming to know that the funds have been misused and misappropriated, the complainant obtained information from the concerned bank and compared it with the audit report submitted to the Registrar and in both the reports, irregularities were found.

It was also averred that payment was made to the employees of the trade union from the Balco Management through the contractor, but it is wrongly shown in the audit report that the payment was made from the funds of the trade union, and from the General Body no approval was obtained.
Based on such allegations, FIR has been registered for the aforesaid offences.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per the by-laws, the co- accused Sanjay Kumar Singh and Jay Prakash Yadav were duly authorized to withdraw the amount.
There was dispute about the activities of the trade union.
There were two fractions in the group and the complainant was one of the members of the association belonging to different group.

He further submits that as per the averments made in the FIR, withdrawal can be made as per the direction of the Executive Chairman Sanjay Singh and G. Sanjeeva Reddy and any of the two signatories could withdraw the amount from the account.

If any defalcation or misappropriation was made by the office bearer of the trade union, the members can raise their voice in the general body meeting or Executive Committee meeting or can make a complaint before the competent authority i.e. the Registrar.
He further submits that FIR has been registered without holding any enquiry on the basis of assumption.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that recently 3 different FIRs have been registered against Sanjay Singh and Jai Prakash Yadav with an ulterior motive to destroy their image.
In another FIR, Sanjay Singh and Jai Prakash Yadav have already been released on anticipatory bail.

It is further submitted that complainant Narendra Tiwari and another person, who were the office bearers of the trade union have been punished by way of disciplinary action by the management of the Balco.
The services of the complainant have been terminated.
As per Central Trade Union Regulations, 1938, clause-15 audit and every payment have to be checked by the auditor appointed in accordance with the regulations.

He further submits that as per Section 33 of the Trade Union Act, 1926, cognizance of offence is barred unless complaint thereof has been made by or with the previous sanction of the Registrar or, in the case of offence under Section 32, by a person to whom the copy was given, within 6 months of the date on which offence is alleged to have been committed.
Apparently, in this matter, no such sanction has been obtained and registration of offence itself is bad in law.

He also submits that the co-accused namely Sanjay Kumar Singh and Jay Prakash Yadav have already been granted anticipatory bail by the coordinate bench of this Court vide order dated 11.08.2023 in M.Cr.C.(A) No. 869/2023 & M.Cr.C.(A) No. 871/2023.
The present applicant shall abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while granting the bail.
Therefore, the present applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
5. Per contra, learned State Counsel and learned counsel for the Objector would oppose the bail application.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the Objector submits that the applicant has given wrong information to the auditor and the auditor without verifying and comparing the bank statements accepted the disclosure made by the applicant concerning details of expenditure.
When the said fact came to the fore, the FIR has been lodged.

7. Considering the submissions of the parties, particularly considering the fact that there is specific provision about cognizance of offence; the complainant is also holding the post of office bearer and he is one of the authorized signatories for withdrawal of the amount from the account of the trade union; there is no such bar for the complainant to bring such facts to the notice of the members of the Executive Committee and to call a General Body meeting and take appropriate legal course as available to him as per the bye-laws of the trade union and to file a complaint before the competent authority; further considering that there is conflicting interest between the two fractions of the group which led to several litigation between them and it ultimately turned into an ugly colour of an FIR, though representatives of the trade unions are bound to protect the interest of members of the union and also considering that the facts alleged are documentary, there is no chance of tampering with the evidence and the co-accused namely Sanjay Kumar Singh and Jay Prakash Yadav have already been granted anticipatory bail by the coordinate bench of this Court, this Court is inclined to release the present applicant on anticipatory bail.

8. Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest of applicant in connection with crime in question, he shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting him on his executing a personal bond in sum of Rs.50,000/- to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

Applicant shall also abide by following conditions:-
(i) he shall not influence the witnesses during trial.
(ii) he shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.

(iii) he shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such fact to the Court or Investigating Officer, as the case may be.

(iv) he shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial, and (v) after filing of the charge sheet, he shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
9. The observation made in the course of this order is only for considering the case of applicant on the application for grant of anticipatory bail.
The concerned trial Court shall not be influenced or bound by the observation made in the course of this order.
